title: Granada CF and Mallorca clash in Spanish Second Division
seoTitle: Granada CF and Mallorca clash in Spanish Second Division
subtitle: Teams meet this Monday in opposite table positions after the opening round.
excerpt: All the details on the Granada CF vs Mallorca second‑round showdown, including likely line‑ups, stats and broadcast options.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Granada CF takes the field this Monday, August 24, 2026, to face Mallorca in the second round of the Spanish Second Division. The match, scheduled for 4:30 p.m. (Brasília time) at Nuevo Los Cármenes Stadium, pits two sides that opened the campaign in very different ways. While the hosts are looking to score their first goal, the visitors aim to keep their early momentum.

How the teams arrive for the clash

Granada CF debuted in the competition with a goalless draw against Oviedo away from home, temporarily placing them 16th in the table with one point. Mallorca, on the other hand, sits 8th with three points after a 2‑0 home win over Real Valladolid, with goals from Raíllo and Pablo Torre. Recent head‑to‑head records favor Granada, which has won seven of the last ten meetings, while Mallorca has won two and one match ended in a draw.

Granada’s recent home form

For the home duel, Granada is counting on the home‑field factor to improve on last season’s record, when they finished 14th in the promotion division with 48 points. Under coach Pacheta, the side boasts a run of four unbeaten games in their last five matches in Granada. The team’s strength has been its defence, conceding an average of only 0.60 goals per game in this recent home stretch. The main offensive hopes for the match are number 10 Chinaza Marvellous and striker Sergio Rodelas.

The strength of Mallorca after a victorious debut

Mallorca, led by Luis García, arrives buoyed by solid tactical organisation and defensive stability shown in the first round, when they kept a clean sheet. The side, which played in the top tier last season, averages 1.90 goals per game over the last ten matches, registering 4.7 shots on target per contest. However, their away record raises a warning flag: they avoided defeat in only one of their last five official away games last season, conceding an average of 1.80 goals per away match.

Probable line‑ups and absences

Neither team has confirmed injuries or suspensions for Monday’s clash. Granada is expected to repeat the 4‑3‑3 formation used in the opener, fielding Raúl Lizoáin, Sergio López, Bourama Dembele, Manu Lama, Baïla Diallo, Rubén Alcaraz, Gerard Gumbau, Pedro Alemán, Sergio Rodelas, Chinaza Okonyia and José Arnáiz. Mallorca should also stick to the 4‑4‑2 set‑up that delivered the opening‑round win, with Arnau Tenas, Miguel Calatayud, Antonio Raíllo, Martin Valjent, Toni Lato, Zito Luvumbo, Sergi Darder, Manu Morlanes, Antoniu Roca, Adrián Fuentes and Pablo Torre.

Where to watch the game in Brazil

The Granada CF vs Mallorca match will not have an official television broadcast or streaming platform confirmed for Brazil. Fans who want to follow the action live can turn to authorised betting‑site streams. The game is slated to kick off at 4:30 p.m. Brasília time, directly from Nuevo Los Cármenes Stadium in Granada, Spain.

Information from Rádio Itatiaia, ogol.com.br.
